subject: Capacity wedge probe for SignalForge Dedicated commitment
messages:
From: Sara Mendes <sara@signalforge.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: tom.ellis@signalforge.com
Date: Sun, 21 Jul 2029 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing — initial traffic snapshot for SignalForge pilot

Olga / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. Per our discussion, SignalForge is evaluating a dedicated capacity commitment to power an in-prod recommender and conversational assistant for our analytics product. We have a tight pilot window (Q3 -> early Q4) and want to size for a conservative baseline + a 3x burst buffer.

Initial asks from our side: can you validate whether a dedicated pool of ~6 A100-class GPUs is reasonable, and what expected p99 latency and token cost would be for our workload? Below is a short summary of the traffic we can share now — more detailed telemetry forthcoming from our infra team (Tom).

- Peak concurrent sessions (interactive): 120 (95th percentile day)
- Average prompt length: 60 tokens
- Average model-generated response length: 420 tokens
- Percentage of requests that are multimodal (images + text): ~8% (handled by separate pipeline)
- Percent critical low-latency flows (dashboard queries): ~25% of requests (p99 target 350ms)
- Typical tails: short bursts of ~20–30% above baseline for 5–10 minutes, once or twice per day

We can share a sample token distribution CSV from our telemetry team later today — tagging Tom on this thread. Primary goal: a SLO-aware sizing recommendation and a list of questions that will let us finalize a reserved capacity proposal.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Mendes
Head of Platform 
SignalForge Ltd

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Sara Mendes <sara@signalforge.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@signalforge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing — initial traffic snapshot for SignalForge pilot

Sara — thanks for the summary and the context. This is very helpful.

Quick notes up front: 6 A100s could be in the right ballpark depending on model family (fp16 vs quantized), concurrency pattern (many short requests vs fewer long ones), and how much KV-cache reuse we can get for conversational sessions. We’ll need the token distribution and an example prompt mix to make an apples-to-apples projection.

Next steps I suggest (short checklist):
- Tom: please share the token distribution CSV and a small sample of 50–100 representative prompts/responses (anonymized).
- SignalForge: confirm the model family you expect to serve (open Llama2 variants, mix of 13B / 70B, or a hosted-proprietary model).
- Redwood: we’ll run a quick back-of-envelope throughput map and follow with a conservative sizing suggestion and p99 latency envelope for the given SLOs.

I’ll kick a short preflight questionnaire below so we can capture the edge cases that drive dedicated sizing. If you prefer a quick workshop, Marissa and Karthik can run a focused sizing session this week.

Preflight intake (please fill or attach):
1) Traffic cadence: expected sustained QPS and 95th/99th percentile peak windows (per hour/day).
2) Session affinity: average session length (minutes) and whether users tend to have multiple turns in one session (KV cache reuse).
3) Prompt/response mix: percent of under-100-token prompts vs over-500-token responses.
4) Burst characteristics: frequency, duration, and whether bursts are synchronous across customers or user-driven.
5) Fallback & degradation policy: acceptable fallbacks (lower-capacity model, queueing) during extreme overload.
6) Telemetry access: a shared DocSend or S3 link with token histograms and example payloads.

If you can get those artifacts to us by EOD Wed (24 Jul), we’ll aim to circulate a sizing sketch and a recommended dedicated pool configuration (including a burst lane plan).

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, Sara Mendes <sara@signalforge.com>, tom.ellis@signalforge.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jul 2029 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing — initial traffic snapshot for SignalForge pilot

Looping in a couple of artifacts while we wait for the full telemetry: attaching a minimal token-sample template (signalforge_token_sample.csv) and our dedicated preflight checklist (redwood_dedicated_preflight_checklist.pdf).

Notes and immediate asks from pre-sales ops:
- Karthik: quick input — if SignalForge plans to use 70B-class models for the assistant and 13B for lightweight reranking, how would you recommend splitting a 6-node fleet vs recommending different skus?
- SignalForge: please flag any regulatory constraints (data residency, retention windows) that would affect Private vs Dedicated placement.

Marissa (cc: Laura who will surface SLO/contract implications when we get sizing).

—Marissa Cole
Director, Pre-Sales Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: signalforge_token_sample.csv (CSV — token counts by request), redwood_dedicated_preflight_checklist.pdf (PDF — intake checklist)
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@signalforge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: sara@signalforge.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2029 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing — initial traffic snapshot for SignalForge pilot

Thanks — attaching the telemetry sample (see DocSend link). We ran a quick export with token histograms and session lengths. High level clarifications:
- Model family: primary is an fp16 LLaMA-2-70B variant for the assistant; we use a 13B quantized model for lightweight ranking/filters.
- Typical session turn count: median 3 turns, 95th percentile 11 turns (KV cache reuse expected).
- Recent peak daycare: sustained 80 QPS for ~8 minutes during one release test; production peaks we expect ~120 concurrent interactive sessions as Sara noted.
- Retention/regulatory: all EU PII is routed to our regional cluster; US production is fine on dedicated in us-west.

DocSend: https://docsend.com/view/signalforge-telemetry
HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood/deals/SF-2029-042

If you can sketch a conservative 90-day pilot configuration and a recommended burst lane (hot spare capacity or autoscale policy + expected cost delta), that would be ideal for our procurement briefing next week.

Tom
Tom Ellis
Principal SRE, SignalForge Ltd
